Wedding shuttle bus in Scottsdale: seats, rates and loops

Scottsdale Sprinters runs wedding shuttle bus service for the guests: an executive class seating 8 to 56 that loops between the hotel districts, the ceremony and the reception on a booked block of hours. Published rates are $145 to $325 per hour on a 4-hour minimum, and 5 on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach, so a wedding shuttle starts between $580 and $1,625 before tax with Arizona sales tax of 8% added at checkout. Below: how many guests fit, how many loops or coaches a guest list needs, where the shuttle waits, the late-night return, and what it works out at per guest.

Last updated: September 26, 2026

What is a wedding shuttle bus in Scottsdale?

A chauffeured guest shuttle, booked for a block of hours to move wedding guests between the hotels, the ceremony and the reception. The class Scottsdale Sprinters books for it seats 8 to 56 at $145 to $325 per hour on a 4-hour minimum, the same class a corporate shuttle books. Forward-facing seats in rows, moving the guests who are not in the wedding party: rooms to ceremony, ceremony to reception, and back to the rooms at the end of the night. Nothing here is a seat sale. You reserve the vehicle and the chauffeur for the hours, so 24 guests and 29 guests pay the same for the same Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax).

How many guests fit on a wedding shuttle bus?

Between 8 and 56 a trip, depending on the unit. Scottsdale Sprinters seats 24 on the Mini Bus (24 Pax), 27 on the Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax), 29 on the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) and 56 on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach; the executive Sprinters under them take 8 to 14. Every count is a seated count: nobody rides standing. Past 56 there is nothing larger in this fleet: the guest shuttle becomes a coordinated fleet on one reservation, and two shuttles can leave two hotel districts at once.

How do you size a guest shuttle against the guest count?

Count the guests who actually need the ride, not the guest list. Scottsdale Sprinters sizes from the riders staying in one hotel district, then takes the smallest unit that clears them, in seat order: the Mini Bus (24 Pax), the Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax), the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax), then the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. Local guests drive themselves; the out-of-town guests are the shuttle list, and in practice that is the room block, a number the couple can count instead of guess. Old Town Scottsdale, North Scottsdale and Paradise Valley are three different drives, so a room block split across two of them is two pickups. The quote is written against those addresses.

How many loops or coaches does a guest list need?

Divide the riders by the seats and round up. For 100 guests, Scottsdale Sprinters runs 4 loops of one Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax), 5 loops of one Mini Bus (24 Pax), or 2 coaches in a single wave on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. A wave is everyone at once and needs seats for the whole list. A loop is one vehicle running the same leg repeatedly, a smaller vehicle for a longer booking, and often for less, because you pay for hours, not seats. The shapes mix: the ceremony run suits a wave, because everyone has to be seated together, and the return suits a loop, because guests leave in groups. Ask for both in one quote.

How far apart do the shuttle loops run?

One round trip apart. A loop leaves the pickup full, drops at the venue and comes back empty for the next 29 guests on the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax), so the gap between loops is the drive there and back. Scottsdale Sprinters sets it against your two addresses in the written quote. A room block a few streets from the venue turns a loop quickly; a desert venue from the same rooms does not, and there a second vehicle usually beats extra loops. Give the first ready time and the time the last guest must be seated; the quote states how many loops fit between them, or prices a second shuttle.

Where does the shuttle wait at the ceremony and the reception?

Where the venue tells commercial vehicles to go. Put that instruction on the booking and the chauffeur works from it. On an hourly booking the Scottsdale Sprinters shuttle stays with you for the 4-hour minimum or longer, so it is staged for the next run rather than sent away. Write every address on the reservation as its own movement (the hotels, the ceremony, the reception) rather than one round trip with implied stops. Name one point person the chauffeur calls on the day, someone other than the couple: a planner, a coordinator or a groomsman holding the guest manifest.

How does the late-night return to the hotels work?

It rides on the same hourly booking. Stops inside the booked hours cost nothing, and time beyond them bills at the same published rate rather than a penalty rate. Scottsdale Sprinters runs the last loop back to the rooms, and more than one hotel is more than one drop on the 4-hour block. Guests leave in groups, so the return runs as loops, and the last run waits for the last guest. If the only late movement is one run to one hotel, it can be a single transfer instead of more hours; the written quote prices both.

One way, hourly or a loop: which shape do you book?

Three shapes. Hourly is the vehicle staying with you for a booked block, on a 4-hour minimum and 5 on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. A loop is that same booking spent running one leg repeatedly. A single one-way move is a transfer instead: $295 in an Executive Black Sprinter, $550 in the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax). A transfer is flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off; longer transfers are priced from the drive with the empty return included. Once the shuttle has to come back for a return, one hourly block usually beats two transfers. The loop saves money on a long list: one Mini Bus (24 Pax) at $185 per hour moves more guests than its 24 seats and starts at $740 before tax, against $1,625 for a 56-Passenger Motorcoach in one wave.

What does a wedding shuttle bus cost per guest?

Divide the booking by the seats. At the minimum, Scottsdale Sprinters shuttles start at $580 to $1,625 before tax, and across the class that splits $29 to $131 a head — the coaches at the bottom, the small executive Sprinters at the top. It is splitting arithmetic, not a per-seat price. About $31 a head on the Mini Bus (24 Pax), $31 on the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) and $29 on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach, each at its own minimum and across every seat. The figure falls as the vehicle fills. The table above prices every unit the same way. Arizona sales tax of 8% is added at checkout, a 50% deposit confirms the date, and the balance is charged to the card on file 48 hours before pickup.

Is the guest shuttle the same booking as the couple’s ride?

No. Scottsdale Sprinters books the couple and the wedding party as their own ride, on the wedding transportation page, and this page covers only the guest shuttle: the 8 to 56 seat executive class above. Send both on one quote request so the two timings are checked against each other. Arrival-day runs carry bags, and bag room is published per unit: 40 on an Executive Black Sprinter, 30 on the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) and 125 on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. The Mini Bus (24 Pax) has no confirmed bag count yet, so suitcases ride on a unit that has one. Send mobility needs with the request (a wheelchair, a walker, a low step or a seat near the door), because vehicles differ and it changes which one fits.

What are the house rules on a wedding shuttle?

Three carry a fee: $1,500 for smoking or vaping on board, because the smell does not leave, $450 to deep-clean an excessive spill and $450 for a biohazard clean. An added stop on a transfer is $50, and nothing else is added to the base fare. Scottsdale Sprinters publishes the full list on the ride rules page. Arizona's rules for alcohol in a chauffeured vehicle have their own page: the Arizona alcohol law guide linked below answers that question for a wedding shuttle too. Aisles, doors and exits stay clear, which matters in formal wear.

How does the written quote work?

Four steps: pick the unit from the table, send the date with every movement on it, confirm with a 50% deposit, and the balance is charged to the card on file 48 hours before pickup. Every figure on this page is the published rate card; your own total comes back in writing. Send the ready time for each movement, the hotel and venue addresses, the number of guests riding, and whether each run is a wave or a loop. Call or text (623) 986-6339, email reservations@scottsdalesprinters.com, or request a current quote on the pricing page; the quote confirms the unit by name, with its rate and minimum.

Maybach Jet Sprinter: seats 9, $295/hr, 4-hour minimum. 4 hours is $1,180 before tax, about $131 per person. Executive Black Sprinter: seats 14, $145/hr, 4-hour minimum. 4 hours is $580 before tax, about $41 per person. Executive White Sprinter: seats 14, $145/hr, 4-hour minimum. 4 hours is $580 before tax, about $41 per person. Mini Bus (24 Pax): seats 24, $185/hr, 4-hour minimum. 4 hours is $740 before tax, about $31 per person. Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax): seats 27, $225/hr, 4-hour minimum. 4 hours is $900 before tax, about $33 per person. Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax): seats 29, $225/hr, 4-hour minimum. 4 hours is $900 before tax, about $31 per person. 56-Passenger Motorcoach: seats 56, $325/hr, 5-hour minimum. Its 5-hour minimum is $1,625 before tax, about $29 per person.

Frequently asked questions

How much do shuttle buses for weddings cost in Scottsdale?

Scottsdale Sprinters publishes guest-shuttle rates of $145 to $325 per hour on a 4-hour minimum. The 56-Passenger Motorcoach carries its own 5-hour minimum, so a wedding shuttle starts between $580 and $1,625 before tax. Arizona sales tax of 8% is added at checkout. Request a current quote for your own date and addresses.

How many guests fit on a wedding shuttle bus?

Scottsdale Sprinters seats 8 to 56 across the shuttle class: 24 on the Mini Bus (24 Pax), 27 on the Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax), 29 on the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) and 56 on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. Every count is a seated count — nobody rides standing.

How many shuttle loops does a wedding guest list need?

Divide the riders by the seats and round up. For 100 guests, Scottsdale Sprinters runs 4 loops of one Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) or 5 of one Mini Bus (24 Pax), or sends 2 coaches in one wave on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. The loops are one round trip apart.

Is there an hourly minimum on a wedding shuttle?

Yes. Every Scottsdale Sprinters shuttle books on a 4-hour minimum, so a booking starts at the published rate times that minimum: $580 before tax in an Executive Black Sprinter, $900 in the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax). The 56-Passenger Motorcoach is the one exception, on its own 5-hour minimum. A single one-way move books as a transfer instead, with no hour count.

What does a wedding shuttle bus cost per guest?

At the minimum and across every seat, Scottsdale Sprinters shuttles split $29 to $131 a head: about $29 on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach and $31 on the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax). You reserve the vehicle rather than the seat, so a half-full shuttle costs the same and the per-head figure rises.

How do wedding shuttles handle more than one hotel?

Scottsdale Sprinters either runs one vehicle on a loop between the two districts or books a second shuttle so both leave at once. Two Mini Bus (24 Pax) units start at $740 each, against $1,625 for one 56-Passenger Motorcoach. Give both addresses and the written quote compares the shapes.

Can the wedding shuttle run guests back to the hotel late at night?

Yes. On an hourly booking Scottsdale Sprinters runs the late-night return as the last loops of the same block: stops inside the booked hours cost nothing, and time beyond them bills at the same published rate. A single run back to one hotel can book as a transfer instead.

Do wedding guest shuttles run in Phoenix as well as Scottsdale?

Yes. Scottsdale Sprinters runs one reservations desk for the whole metro, and the same shuttles, rates and minimums apply — $145 to $325 per hour on a 4-hour minimum. What changes is the itinerary, which is why the quote is written against your own addresses.

How do I book a wedding shuttle bus in Scottsdale?

Request a current quote with your date and every movement on the pricing page, or call or text Scottsdale Sprinters on (623) 986-6339. A 50% deposit confirms the vehicle and the balance is charged to the card on file 48 hours before pickup.
